## concern body carries first lines and log path

ID: `project-graph-refresh/concern-body-carries-first-lines-and-log-path`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The concern body SHALL carry the first line of each problem and the path of the day's log, each passed through `public_text.redact`, and SHALL NOT carry a step's output beyond that first line.

## failure opens one concern

ID: `project-graph-refresh/failure-opens-one-concern`

Status: **implemented and tested**

A run with problems SHALL open (or comment on) the keyed concern `project-graph-refresh` in the configured concern repository through `scripts/concern_issue.py`; a clean run SHALL close it.

Implemented by:

- `project_graph_refresh` — [`scripts/project_graph_refresh.py:1`](../../scripts/project_graph_refresh.py#L1)

## graph lands in settings repo

ID: `project-graph-refresh/graph-lands-in-settings-repo`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The steps SHALL work on a staging copy of the graph. Only when the copy differs from the live graph after the taxonomy check passes SHALL the job copy it over the live file, commit that one file with the configured `git_identity` and `git push origin HEAD:main` in the settings repository, never through a pull request and never forced. The settings repository SHALL be on main and clean before the run (then `pull --ff-only`) and clean after the commit; otherwise nothing is committed or pushed and the problem is reported, and the page still goes out.

Implemented by:

- `project_graph_refresh` — [`scripts/project_graph_refresh.py:1`](../../scripts/project_graph_refresh.py#L1)

- Scenario `graph-lands-in-settings-repo`: tested by `tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py::test_a_changed_graph_is_committed_and_pushed_to_main_with_the_configured_identity` ([`tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py:120`](../../tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py#L120)), `tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py::test_a_dirty_settings_repo_is_never_committed_or_pushed` ([`tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py:143`](../../tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py#L143))

## no push changes nothing

ID: `project-graph-refresh/no-push-changes-nothing`

Status: **implemented and tested**

With `--no-push` every step SHALL run but nothing SHALL be committed or pushed, the live graph SHALL stay unchanged, and no concern SHALL be opened or closed.

Implemented by:

- `project_graph_refresh` — [`scripts/project_graph_refresh.py:1`](../../scripts/project_graph_refresh.py#L1)

## page goes to data branch

ID: `project-graph-refresh/page-goes-to-data-branch`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The activity snapshot and the page SHALL be rebuilt from the staged graph and pushed to the configured data branch of the page repository (`docs/plans/project_activity.json`, `docs/plans/project-graph.review.html`), never to its main; the data branch starts with no history the first time.

Implemented by:

- `project_graph_refresh` — [`scripts/project_graph_refresh.py:1`](../../scripts/project_graph_refresh.py#L1)

- Scenario `page-goes-to-data-branch`: tested by `tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py::test_data_branch_starts_empty_then_adds_commits_without_touching_main` ([`tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py:170`](../../tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py#L170))

## step log

ID: `project-graph-refresh/step-log`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Each step SHALL be timed and appended to one log per day (`project-graph-refresh-YYYY-MM-DD.log`) with its name, command, exit status, seconds and output, in this order: register new repositories, fill `depends_on`, taxonomy check, land the graph, activity snapshot, page, publish. A failed `depends_on` scan SHALL be reported and the run SHALL carry on; any other failed step SHALL stop the run.

Implemented by:

- `project_graph_refresh` — [`scripts/project_graph_refresh.py:1`](../../scripts/project_graph_refresh.py#L1)

- Scenario `step-log`: tested by `tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py::test_refresh_stops_at_the_first_failed_step_and_logs_it` ([`tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py:75`](../../tests/test_project_graph_refresh.py#L75))
